title: State the file's one job in a Purpose: line of at most 80 characters

facts.note: Every implementation (non-test) source file, whether new, edited or unchanged; test files are excluded by the source. No phase, operation, finding or language gate: the obligation is universal over implementation files and stack-neutral.

fires: A new implementation file is created without a `Purpose:` line in its header.
An existing, unchanged implementation file has no `Purpose:` line when the codebase is checked.
An implementation file's `Purpose:` line is 81 or more characters long.
An implementation file's header has a URN line but no `Purpose:` description (reported at the URN line).
doesNotFire: A test file has no `Purpose:` line (test files are excluded).
An implementation file's `Purpose:` line is exactly 80 characters.

given: Any implementation (non-test) file in the codebase
when: its header is authored, changed, or checked
then: The header carries a single `Purpose:` line of at most 80 characters that truthfully names the file's one job.
prefer: During GREEN, derive the purpose from the responsibility introduced for the current acceptance.
Use concrete responsibility language rather than implementation mechanics.
If the purpose genuinely cannot fit because the new file owns multiple jobs, split only the responsibilities required by the current behavior.
avoid: Inventing a vague purpose just to meet the length cap.
Unrelated decomposition: when splitting a file whose purpose does not fit, do not decompose anything beyond the responsibilities the current behavior requires.
unless: The file is a test file (test files are excluded).
why: An unbounded description becomes a paragraph that goes stale and, being believed, is worse than none; the 80-character cap forces naming one job, and a purpose that will not fit usually signals a file doing more than one thing (a design signal as much as a documentation rule).
evidence: The detector reports no missing or over-length `Purpose:` finding for the file.
Reviewer confirms the purpose truthfully names one job and fits the limit.
verifier_detail: Length cap is inclusive: exactly 80 characters passes; 81 does not.
A missing `Purpose:` description is reported at the header's URN line.
Test files are excluded from the check.
Realized by `bun_green_traceability_detector` (implementation type: validator); finding aliases GREEN-HEADER-002 (core alias) and BUN-GREEN-HEADER-PURPOSE-001.
audit: schema_version 1.1.0; kind rule; status active; introduced_in 0.1.0.
Stack-neutral obligation, Bun-specific detector; implementation: {type: validator, ref: bun_green_traceability_detector}.

Source terms: purpose_line = a single `Purpose:` line of at most 80 characters stating the file's one job; length_cap = the 80-character limit, which forces one job to be named, and a purpose that will not fit is evidence the file has more than one.
Source summary: a 'one-line purpose' obligation: present, and 80 characters or fewer. 'The 80-character cap is the whole rule.'

sharedNodes.text: Prove: the current behavioral acceptance passes.
Disposition strict: fails on every finding, no advisory mode, no ratchet baseline.
